prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Education / social science
Problem: Why do a few students from identical schools and backgrounds thrive despite an intervention or adversity that derails most others?
How it is studied: Researchers use longitudinal cohort studies and positive-deviance analysis to identify outliers. They conduct qualitative interviews and mixed-methods work to find hidden factors such as mentors and routines. They also use randomized trials and propensity-score matching to test whether those factors cause the outcomes.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded longitudinal cohort tracking of persister fates
ideas.description: Tag cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population into replicate pools before drug, and sequence barcodes at several timepoints. This tests whether survival is pre-existing and heritable (the same barcodes surviving across replicates) or stochastic, as cohort studies do when following individuals over time.

ideas.title: Positive-deviance single-cell profiling of pre-treatment survivors
ideas.description: Use barcode-matched sister cells, or live-cell reporters with sorting, to profile the pre-drug transcriptome, chromatin state and signaling of cells that later prove to be survivors. Comparing them with matched non-survivors from the same culture identifies the hidden factors, such as a drug-efflux or stress-response state, that predate treatment.

ideas.title: Time-lapse single-cell tracking with retrospective outcome linkage
ideas.description: Image fluorescent reporters of cell cycle, ERK/AKT activity, and mitochondrial or redox state continuously before and after drug, then link each cell's history to its fate. Mixed-methods logic applies here: dynamic traces generate hypotheses about routines such as slow cycling or pulsatile signaling that distinguish survivors.

ideas.title: Matched-control causal perturbation of candidate survival factors
ideas.description: Take candidate factors from the profiling, such as a state marker or regulator, and perturb them by CRISPRi/a or drug in a randomized, matched design. Compare survivor fractions with propensity-matched or randomized controls, adjusting for cell cycle, size and density, to test whether each factor causes survival rather than merely correlating with it.

ideas.title: Microenvironment-matched neighbor and spatial analysis
ideas.description: Use spatial transcriptomics or imaging to compare survivors with non-survivors in matched local neighborhoods, controlling for density, nutrient gradients and paracrine signals. Controlling these 'identical school' conditions separates cell-intrinsic state from local context, and a co-culture or conditioned-medium experiment can then test the contextual factors.
